items.title: Local periodic incompressible model evolution
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Force-free smooth constant-density incompressible Newtonian model on a periodic cell; constant nonnegative shear viscosity; local smooth evolution in dimensions 1, 2, and 3. The zero-viscosity branch is inviscid Euler. No walls, variable-viscosity evolution, thermal equation, or empirical validation is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $L>0$, $U_*>0$, and $ho_*>0$, and fix an integer $s\ge4$. Use SI units: $L$ is measured in metres, $U_*$ in metres per second, physical position $X$ in metres, time $t$ in seconds, mass density $ho_*$ in kilograms per cubic metre, velocity $u$ in metres per second, pressure $p$ and stress $\sigma$ in pascals, and dynamic shear viscosity $\mu$ in pascal seconds. Let the physical periodic cell be $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/(2\pi L\mathbb Z))^d$. Adopt a force-free incompressible Newtonian model with constant density $ho_*$, constant shear viscosity $\mu\ge0$, velocity field $u$, pressure multiplier $p$ enforcing $
abla_X\cdot u=0$, and stress
$$\sigma=-pI+2\mu D_Xu,\qquad D_Xu=	frac12 igl(
abla_Xu+(
abla_Xu)^{\mathsf T} igr).$$
The local momentum equation and incompressibility constraint are
$$ho_* igl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot
abla_X)u igr)=
abla_X\cdot\sigma,\qquad 
abla_X\cdot u=0.$$
Assume $u_0:\mathbb T_L^d	o\mathbb R^d$ is smooth, real, periodic, and divergence-free. Set $x=X/L\in\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z))^d$, $	au=tU_*/L$, $U_0(x)=u_0(Lx)/U_*$, $ ar
u=\mu/(ho_*U_*L)$, and $\Pi=p/(ho_*U_*^2)$. For a smooth periodic field $f$, use normalized measure $d\mu_x=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$, coefficients $\widehat f(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu_x$, and
$$\|f\|_{H^s}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}(1+|k|^2)^s|\widehat f(k)|^2.$$
For this integer $s$, there is $T>0$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $\|U_0\|_{H^s}$, and independent of $ ar
u$ and all higher Sobolev norms of $U_0$, such that the normalized system has a unique smooth solution $(U,\Pi)$ on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^d$:
$$\partial_	au U+(U\cdot
abla_x)U=-
abla_x\Pi+ ar
u\Delta_xU,\qquad 
abla_x\cdot U=0,\qquad U(0,\cdot)=U_0,$$
with $\Pi$ fixed by zero spatial mean at each time. Every integer Sobolev order $m\ge s$ remains bounded on this same interval. Returning to physical variables gives a unique smooth model evolution on $0\le t\le (L/U_*)T$. When $\mu=0$, the adopted stress is $-pI$ and the model is inviscid Euler; when $\mu>0$, it is viscous Navier–Stokes. This is a conditional model deduction and makes no claim of empirical validity, wall evolution, variable-viscosity evolution, or thermal evolution.

references.title: Brian F. Morton, Local-in-Time Well-Posedness of the Incompressible Euler and Navier–Stokes Equations
references.locator: §§7.1–7.3, especially Theorem 7.5, PDF pp. 24–34; whole-space mollifier method, compared only for scope.

references.title: Emil Wiedemann, Lecture Notes — Navier–Stokes Equations
references.locator: §4.3, Lemma 4.13 and Theorem 4.14, PDF pp. 31–32; positive-viscosity 3D-torus local strong-solution treatment.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 2
references.locator: §§3.1.1–3.1.2, PDF pp. 59–63; stress formulation and kinetic-energy balance context.

references.title: Sergei Kuksin and Armen Shirikyan, Mathematics of Two-Dimensional Turbulence
references.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.1.5–2.1.7, PDF pp. 42–51; independent periodic energy/regularity context.

items.title: Local positive-density polytropic model evolution
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Unforced, smooth, positive-density, isentropic barotropic Euler model on a periodic cell, with one fixed polytropic parameter and exponent. It asserts local smooth evolution and conservation of the mean total energy density. It does not cover vacuum, shocks, thermal coupling, variable entropy parameters, or a molecular derivation of the constitutive law.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $L>0$, reference density $\rho_*>0$ in kilograms per cubic metre, reference speed $U_*>0$ in metres per second, physical polytropic coefficient $\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}>0$ in pascals times $(\mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{kg})^\gamma$, and dimensionless exponent $\gamma>1$. Let the physical periodic cell be $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/(2\pi L\mathbb Z))^d$, with position $X$ in metres and time $t$ in seconds. The physical density $\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}$ is measured in kilograms per cubic metre, velocity $u_{\mathrm{phys}}$ in metres per second, and pressure $p_{\mathrm{phys}}$ in pascals. Adopt the unforced, positive-density barotropic Euler model
$$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}+\nabla_X\cdot(\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}u_{\mathrm{phys}})=0,\qquad \partial_tu_{\mathrm{phys}}+(u_{\mathrm{phys}}\cdot\nabla_X)u_{\mathrm{phys}}+\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}^{-1}\nabla_X\!\left(\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}^\gamma\right)=0,$$
where the same fixed $\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}$ and $\gamma$ apply throughout the flow. Set $x=X/L\in\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z))^d$, $\tau=tU_*/L$, $R=\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}/\rho_*$, $V=u_{\mathrm{phys}}/U_*$, $P=p_{\mathrm{phys}}/(\rho_*U_*^2)$, and $\bar\kappa=\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_*^{\gamma-1}/U_*^2>0$. Put $a=(\gamma-1)/2$ and $r(R)=\sqrt{\bar\kappa\gamma}\,R^a/a$. For smooth periodic $f$, use normalized measure $d\mu_x=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$, Fourier coefficients $\widehat f(k)=\int f(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu_x$, and $\|f\|_{H^m}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}(1+|k|^2)^m|\widehat f(k)|^2$. Let $\rho_0:\mathbb T_L^d\to(0,\infty)$ and $u_0:\mathbb T_L^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be smooth real periodic initial data, and define $R_0(x)=\rho_0(Lx)/\rho_*$ and $V_0(x)=u_0(Lx)/U_*$. Then for every integer $s\ge4$ there is $T>0$, depending only on $d,s,\bar\kappa,\gamma,\|(r(R_0),V_0)\|_{H^s}$, and $\min r(R_0)$, such that the normalized system
$$\partial_\tau R+\nabla_x\cdot(RV)=0,\qquad \partial_\tau V+(V\cdot\nabla_x)V+R^{-1}\nabla_x(\bar\kappa R^\gamma)=0,\qquad R(0,\cdot)=R_0,\quad V(0,\cdot)=V_0$$
has a unique smooth real solution on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d$ with $R(\tau,x)>0$ and every integer Sobolev order $m\ge s$ bounded on that same interval. The dimensionless mean total-energy density
$$\overline E(\tau)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\left(\tfrac12 R|V|^2+\frac{\bar\kappa}{\gamma-1}R^\gamma\right)d\mu_x$$
is constant. Equivalently, the physical mean of $\tfrac12\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}|u_{\mathrm{phys}}|^2+\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}^\gamma/(\gamma-1)$ over the physical cell is constant and has units of pascals. The polytropic pressure law is an adopted constitutive closure, not a molecular derivation. No thermal equation, vacuum, shock continuation, nonuniform-entropy model, or empirical validity claim is included.

references.title: François Golse, The Boltzmann Equation and Its Hydrodynamic Limits, §7.4
references.locator: Theorem 7.8, PDF pp. 84–86; local symmetrizable compressible Euler context, not the exact periodic barotropic proof.

references.title: Thomas C. Sideris, Formation of Singularities in Three-Dimensional Compressible Fluids
references.locator: §1, PDF pp. 2–3; positive-density local C1 symmetric-hyperbolic existence is cited, not proved, and used only as context.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 3
references.locator: §4.5, PDF pp. 170–171; compressible energy density and flux context.

items.title: Global two-dimensional periodic viscous model evolution
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Force-free smooth constant-density incompressible Newtonian model on a two-dimensional periodic cell, with constant positive shear viscosity. It asserts global smooth evolution for every smooth divergence-free datum inside this adopted planar model. It does not assert 3D or inviscid global regularity, wall evolution, or empirical validity.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $L>0$ be measured in metres, $U_*>0$ in metres per second, $ho_*>0$ be a constant mass density in kilograms per cubic metre, and $\mu>0$ be a constant dynamic shear viscosity in pascal seconds. Use SI position $X$ in metres, time $t$ in seconds, velocity $u$ in metres per second, and pressure $p$ in pascals. On the two-dimensional periodic cell $\mathbb T_L^2=(\mathbb R/(2\pi L\mathbb Z))^2$, adopt the force-free incompressible Newtonian model
$$ho_* igl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot
abla_X)u igr)=
abla_X\cdot\sigma,\qquad 
abla_X\cdot u=0,\qquad \sigma=-pI+2\mu D_Xu,\qquad D_Xu=	frac12 igl(
abla_Xu+(
abla_Xu)^{\mathsf T} igr).$$
Set $x=X/L\in\mathbb T^2=(\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z))^2$, $	au=tU_*/L$, $U=u/U_*$, $\Pi=p/(ho_*U_*^2)$, and $ ar
u=\mu/(ho_*U_*L)>0$. Use normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-2}dx$ and fix the pressure gauge by $\int_{\mathbb T^2}\Pi(	au,x)\,d\mu(x)=0$ at each time. For any smooth real periodic divergence-free initial velocity $U_0:\mathbb T^2	o\mathbb R^2$, the adopted model has a unique smooth velocity $U$ and the unique pressure $\Pi$ with this zero-mean gauge on all normalized times $	au\ge0$, satisfying
$$\partial_	au U+(U\cdot
abla_x)U=-
abla_x\Pi+ ar
u\Delta_xU,\qquad 
abla_x\cdot U=0,\qquad U(0,\cdot)=U_0.$$
Here global means smooth on $[0,\infty)$ with finite Sobolev norms on every compact time interval; no uniform-in-time norm bound is asserted. Scaling back gives a unique global smooth physical model evolution for all $t\ge0$. This conclusion is restricted to the adopted two-dimensional positive-viscosity periodic model; it establishes no three-dimensional or inviscid global regularity result and no empirical validity claim.

references.title: Sergei Kuksin and Armen Shirikyan, Mathematics of Two-Dimensional Turbulence
references.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.1.5–2.1.7, especially Theorem 2.1.18 and its complete regularity estimate, PDF pp. 42–51.

items.title: Homogeneous translating polytropic fluid
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Exact spatially homogeneous positive-density state of the unforced polytropic Euler model on a periodic cell. It makes no thermal, molecular, shock, or empirical claim.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ and let $L>0$ be measured in metres, so the physical periodic cell is $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/(2\pi L\mathbb Z))^d$ with position $X$ in metres and time $t$ in seconds. In SI units, choose a constant density $\rho_*>0$ kilograms per cubic metre, a constant velocity vector $V_*\in\mathbb R^d$ in metres per second, a constant $\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}>0$ in pascals times $(\mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{kg})^\gamma$, and a dimensionless exponent $\gamma>1$. In the unforced polytropic Euler model with pressure $p_{\mathrm{phys}}=\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}^\gamma$, take initial data $\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}(0,X)=\rho_*$ and $u_{\mathrm{phys}}(0,X)=V_*$. The fields $\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}(t,X)=\rho_*$, $u_{\mathrm{phys}}(t,X)=V_*$, and $p_{\mathrm{phys}}(t,X)=\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_*^\gamma$ form a smooth solution for every $t\ge0$. Its total energy density $\tfrac12\rho_*|V_*|^2+\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_*^\gamma/(\gamma-1)$, measured in pascals, is constant in space and time. The unique local solution branch for these data is this homogeneous translating state.
